title: How the Myles Garrett Trade Impacts the Ravens | Baltimore Ravens Final Drive
text: Myles Garrett is out of the AFC North. A blockbuster trade rocked the NFL today as the Browns traded Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams. Here's my reaction to the move and how it impacts the Ravens. Garrett's not only the reigning Defensive Player of the Year, but he also set the single-season sack record last season. He has the most career sacks of any active player in the NFL. Even at 30 years old, Garrett is still a freak of nature that is in the prime of his career. And he's been a thorn in the Ravens' side. In two games last season against Baltimore, he had five and a half sacks and 12 pressures. In 16 career games against the Ravens, he had 14 sacks. Getting Garrett out of the AFC North means no longer facing him twice a season. Garrett and Ravens left tackle Ronnie Stanley had many good battles over the years, but you have to think Stanley is smiling somewhere. Now, on the flip side, the Browns got a haul for trading Garrett. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, the Browns are getting young star pass rusher Jared Verse, a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 second-round pick, and 2029 third-round pick. Now, Verse is a good player in his own regard. He's been a Pro Bowler each of his two years in the league, and he was the AP Defensive Rookie of the Year in 2024. He had seven and a half sacks last year, and only Garrett and Micah Parsons have had more quarterback pressures since Verse entered the league. In the Ravens game against the Rams last year, Verse had a sack, two tackles for loss, and four quarterback hits. He's a very strong player in his own right and 25 years old, so a lot of years against him for the Ravens most likely. Now, the Browns are stocking up with more draft picks as they build for the future. That 2027 first-round pick will most likely be a late one, however. The Rams have now vaulted ahead of the Ravens as Vegas' favorite to win next year's Super Bowl. The Ravens landed a premier pass rusher in Trey Hendrickson this offseason. The Browns shipped one out in exchange for an up-and-coming talent and draft picks. The AFC North continues to make big moves and we just kicked off June. What's coming next? That's it for me on Final Drive and we'll be back with you tomorrow.

title: Spurs Analyst Sean Elliott Talks Wembanyama, NBA Finals & More with Rich Eisen | Full Interview
text: Perfect guy to speak with right now as the Spurs are back in the NBA Finals. Um and uh the last time they won it all was 1999 when they took on guess who, the New York Knicks. It's perfect uh a word, I think, arrival for this squad, Sean. >> Yeah, it's fitting, right? Because it's also about an alien movie and first contact. >> [laughter] >> Good one. >> Yeah, Victor. Yeah, you have Victor Wembanyama who is the alien. He has arrived and look, I I thought going into this year, I thought we were a mid-50 win team. Uh we we didn't have Victor for the last 18 games last year. Uh missed De'Aaron Fox for the last 60 or so. He had uh finger surgery. And so I I was thinking, you know, we're we're a 50-win team or so, but halfway through the season, when I saw other teams go through or when we were winning games on the road convincingly, I thought, you know, quietly, you know, we we we have a we have a chance. I thought next year next year we're going to be a team that's going to contend for a title. I I just uh didn't see this coming. And I I don't think anybody in San Antonio saw this coming. All right, I thought we were going to be a really good team, but the way our guys have gelled and grown up before our very eyes here. Uh we talked about the inexperience of this ball club all year long, but when you go into a game seven on the road against the defending champion and the two-time MVP and you win that way, the win that game the way they did uh late down the stretch making plays. Uh this team has grown up. They have arrived. They're here and they're going to be a problem for a long, long time. >> Why do you think this is happening right now? >> I I think number one, I think Miss Johnson's done an unbelievable job. I said it over and over again, Rich. I don't think people were listening. He was the coach of the year. Where ESPN projected us went 40 games, we won 62. 62. So, uh he did a phenomenal job getting everybody to believe in each other, uh getting everybody to play on the defensive end of the floor. The hardest thing in this league to do is to get young teams to defend. Everybody's trying to get their numbers. No one's trying to stop anybody. Our guys went out there, accepted the their roles, and they defended their butts off the entire year. So, Mitch Johnson, I think is the number one reason uh we have ascended to the highest and Brian Wright has to be commended as well. I thought again, he was the executive of the year. I thought the signing of Luke Kornet this summer was uh the biggest signing of the summer. It flew under the radar, but he's been absolutely phenomenal for us. Uh you got De'Aaron Fox uh coming in last year, even though it wasn't this year, you got him last year at the trade deadline. And then you draft Dylan Harper and Carter Bryant. And Dylan Harper, I've been telling people he's a superstar. He is an absolute superstar. No doubt about it. Uh he's uh plays well beyond his years. He plays with a lot of poise. Uh he's >> [clears throat] >> never, ever rattled even when things aren't going his way. Uh at this after the second half of the season of the second half of the season, he was probably our best three-point shooter, and that includes having a guy like Julian Champagnie on our team. Uh he defends. He's bigger than most people know, and he finishes extremely well at the basket. And then, you know, Steph Castle has, you know, continued to build on his Rookie of the Year campaign. He's been absolute dog on both ends of the floor. And then you have Devin and and Keldon who have matured and become a valuable team leaders on this team. And then you have of course Victor Wembanyama that anchors and pulls all that together. Now he's an absolute terror on the defensive end of the floor. His offensive game is still coming around.
